• Lighthouses: Beacons of the Edge

  There is something deeply human about a lighthouse. Standing at the boundary
  between land and sea, between safety and catastrophe, it performs one of the
  oldest and most elemental acts of civilization: it says, here is where you
  are, and here is the danger. In a world before GPS, before radio, before any
  of the invisible technologies we now take for granted, the lighthouse was the
  difference between a ship making port and a ship breaking apart on rocks in
  the dark.

  The history of lighthouses stretches back further than most people realize.
  The Pharos of Alexandria, built around 280 BC on a small island off the
  Egyptian coast, is considered the first great lighthouse of the ancient world.
  Standing perhaps 100 meters tall, it was one
